The tests were added by PR #1754 (commit `e16e2d9e`), "(test) Add regression tests for 401 Location-header redirect in openmrsFetch", under ticket O3-5629. They guard the 401 redirect logic in `openmrsFetch` that O3-4897 introduced, so a future change can't silently break it.

**Why:** The PR body says it adds two regression tests for the 401-redirect path. Reviewer ibacher asked for the branch to contain only the tests. Before this, nothing exercised the 401 branch's two fallbacks.

**What the new tests pin down** (all in `openmrs-esm-core/packages/framework/esm-api/src/openmrs-fetch.test.ts`):
- **401 with a `Location` header** (lines 166-185): with `redirectAuthFailure.url` blank, `navigate` is called with `{ to: <Location value> }`, e.g. an auth-module challenge at `/module/authentication/login.form`.
- **401 without a `Location` header** (lines 197-214): with the URL blank and no header, `navigate` falls back to the default auth-failure page, asserted as the literal `'${openmrsSpaBase}/login'` (the template string is passed through unexpanded).

The implementation under test is the branch at `openmrs-esm-core/packages/framework/esm-api/src/openmrs-fetch.ts:225-243`. It navigates to `redirectAuthFailure.url || location || defaultRedirectAuthFailureUrl`. Note that a non-blank configured URL takes precedence over the `Location` header. The configured-URL case was already covered by an older test at lines 216-233, and the `rejectAuthFailure` path is at lines 235-243.

The implementation itself came from O3-4897 (commit `e31fe71d`, PR #1430), which the new tests protect.
